speaker: Kimi K3
text: ICICI Bank's Q2 net income grew 22% year-over-year to ₹163.3 billion on 16% revenue growth, and the last three quarters show a clean earnings beat streak with 4-9% surprises. At 1.6% dividend yield and a 10-year CAGR near 20%, the compounding math works for the long leg of your 10x goal, though the -81% all-time drawdown reminds us why position sizing matters. On the IPO question: with $10 you cannot access Indian IPOs directly — they require INR funding and a demat account — but US-listed ADR IPOs or SPACs are feasible on fractional-share brokers; charges there are just the spread and tiny SEC/FINRA fees. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery: round-trip is ₹38.15 on ₹10,000 (0.38%) including STT, exchange fees, stamp duty, GST and the ₹13.50+GST DP charge, so breakeven is a 0.38% move; short-term gains face 20% tax if sold within 12 months. Auto and battery names like Tata Motors, Mahindra, Exide or Amara Raja fit the rupee budget whole-share requirement — want me to pull fundamentals on any of those next?

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: INTC's 2.13 beta and -82% max drawdown mean a $100 stake can evaporate to $18 in a single bad cycle — the 28.6% worst day in the last two years proves gap risk is real. The 30% EPS surprise last quarter was rewarded with a -31% next-day plunge, so positive fundamentals are being sold aggressively; that's a distribution pattern, not accumulation. With 36 holds and only 12 buys, the Street has zero conviction, and Nvidia's 4% stake looks more like a strategic hedge than a vote of confidence. For a 10x goal, this is a lottery ticket with loaded dice — cash preserves optionality for a cleaner setup.
